summary: Carl Bielefeldt works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Seizan Yanagida, and earned his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley. He served at Stanford University from around 1980 to 2012, becoming emeritus in 2012.

Carl Cappeller (1840–1925) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, at Königsberg, Leipzig (PhD), and Jena (Habilitation). In 1875, he became a professor at the University of Jena.
Carl Christian Rafn (1795–1864) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from around 1814 to 1816 and held a post there from circa 1821 to 1826.

Carl Darling Buck (1866–1955) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Yale University and Leipzig University before serving as a professor at the University of Chicago from 1892 to 1933.

Carl Friedrich Gauss (1777–1855) studied at TU Braunschweig, Göttingen under Lichtenberg and Heyne, and Helmstedt (PhD). From 1807 to 1855, he served as a full professor at the University of Göttingen and director of the Göttingen Observatory.
Carl Gaedicke worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Jena by 1877, having studied under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.

Carl Gustav Jung (1875–1961) was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. After earning a medical degree at the University of Basel, he held posts at the University of Zurich, ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and Basel (1944).

Carl Olson specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under mentor John Y. Fenton and held the Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

Carl Paul Caspari (1814–1892) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and at Berlin. At the University of Oslo, he was appointed lektor in 1847 and professor in 1857.
Carl Schuster (1904–1969) worked in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He pursued his studies at Harvard University from around 1923 to 1930 and at the University of Vienna from around 1930 to 1934.

Carl Shigeo Yamamoto specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, also studying under Sonam Germano, William A. Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

Carl Siegfried (1830–1903) worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Halle, Bonn, and under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He served as professor of Sanskrit at Trinity College Dublin and theological professor at Jena (1875–1901).

Carl W. Ernst (born 1950) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Stanford (A.B.) and Harvard (Ph.D.), he taught at Pomona College (1981–1992) and served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (1876–1967) was a scholar of linguistics and archaeology. Educated in Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin, he served as professor of Greek language and literature at Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht (1917–1946).

Carlo Formichi (1871–1943) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kerbaker, Deussen, Oldenberg, and Bühler, and at Kiel University. He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1898) and Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).

Carlo Giussani (1840–1900) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore from circa 1859 to 1863, and under Giuseppe Bardelli, Albrecht Weber (1863), and Rudolf von Roth (circa 1864–1865).
Carlo Jamelle Harris works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin, attested in 2009.

Carmen Blacker (1924–2009) worked in Japanology and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, Oxford, and Keio University under Shigeru Gorai. She served as Lecturer in Japanese at the University of Cambridge and president of The Folklore Society (1982–1984).

Carmen Dragonetti (1937–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at San Marcos, she was a professor at the University of Buenos Aires (attested 1989) and vice-director of the Fundación Instituto de Estudios Budistas (circa 1989–2018).

Carmen Meinert is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of Bonn in 2001 and held posts at the University of Hamburg, Ruhr University Bochum, and Käte Hamburger Kolleg.
